A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Alterbute by the same authors. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original editing experiments, a 166-participant user study, VLM evaluations, identity-reference ablations, and analyses of its OpenImages-derived VNE clusters.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds commercial-system comparisons, per-attribute results, a conditioning ablation, and training-budget experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed VNE supervision, SDXL-based spatial-grid architecture, diffusion objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Channel-wise conditioning is introduced as an ablation. Appendix G supplies additional inference instructions without establishing a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenImages-derived training clusters and the same 30-object, 100-case evaluation set. Color, texture, material, shape, multi-attribute editing, and joint intrinsic/extrinsic editing already appear in v1. The added experiments do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The original seven comparison methods remain. v2 Appendix C.1 and Table 5 additionally evaluate FluxKontext and Qwen-image-editing, substantially extending the comparison to concurrent systems beyond the original academic baseline set.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 50K-step training condition alongside the retained 100K-step model, including direct comparisons between them, and tests channel-wise versus spatial-grid conditioning. The original benchmark, main training configuration, metrics, and user-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained identity-reference ablation, v2 adds a prose-reported grid-versus-channel ablation, per-attribute performance analysis, and training-budget sensitivity analysis (Section 4.3 and Tables 6–7). These substantially broaden investigation of architectural choices, attribute difficulty, and computational requirements.

E5.justification: Appendix A newly discloses five generated outputs per input for stochastic baselines before best-result selection. This supplies repetition information without establishing an increase in runs. The existing five ratings per case and binomial significance results are unchanged; the added tables provide no new uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The original preference, significance, and DINO/CLIP tables retain their values. New Tables 5–7 report 58.7–62.6% wins against FluxKontext, 49.8–50.3% against Qwen-image-editing, attribute breakdowns, and 75.7–78.0% wins for the 50K-step model against baselines. Figure 6 adds qualitative comparisons, while some older qualitative entries are removed.

T1.justification: The identity formulation, image-formation equations (1)–(3), and diffusion objective (4) are unchanged. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs; the new explanation of grid conditioning is an empirical interpretation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: unified intrinsic-attribute editing with identity preservation, VNE-based supervision, and relaxed training with constrained inference. The main state-of-the-art claim is also retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific limitations concerning Gemini-dependent annotation bias and benchmark size, plus an explicit non-human applicability statement. It also interprets the new conditioning, attribute, and training-budget findings. Existing discussions of attribute dependencies, background artifacts, and rigid-object reshaping remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A and new Table 2 disclose baseline inputs, mask use, absence of task-specific fine-tuning, and best-of-five selection. Appendix G adds mask-prompting guidance and dilation with kernel K=5. These supplement the retained training settings and identical Gemini labeling prompts rather than demonstrate changed implementation.

R1.justification: Section 4.2 drops the explicit first-published-method wording and acknowledges comparable proprietary editors; Appendix C.1 positions Alterbute against two named concurrent systems. Citations to ObjectDrop and Generative Image Layer Decomposition with Visual Effects are removed. Most related-work coverage remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained, with a condensed conclusion and localized edits. v2 adds conflict-of-interest and impact statements, subdivides Appendix C, introduces Appendix G, and replaces numerical citations and generic supplement references with author-year citations and specific cross-references.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a conference layout with running headers and a single-column appendix, adds Tables 2 and 5–7, expands Figures 5–6, and enlarges the questionnaire display. Six supplementary general-comparison grids become three, with some examples relocated into Figure 5. This substantially reorganizes the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The added concurrent-system comparisons, attribute breakdown, and training-budget analysis strengthen assessment of the unchanged method. Clearer baseline and mask documentation and explicit limitations improve transparency. These gains outweigh the reduced qualitative examples, but remain incremental: the benchmark is unchanged, and the new analyses have limited protocol and uncertainty reporting.
